sources: dossier=Net position line 14 (host-agent-and-proxy, 2026-05-24, artifact) 'events fire from the rimsky-side process that owns the state transition's post-commit fan-out'; Required behaviors line 20 (corpus-bootstrap, 2026-06-08, artifact) 'fired synchronously at the corresponding transition ... not fire-and-forget'; doc=lifecycle-subscriber.md invariant (pre-fix line 25) requires synchronous same-process firing; code=instances.go handleTerminateInstance (kill path) marks terminated and closes run scopes synchronously but never calls FanOutInstanceEvent for EventInstanceTerminated itself, leaving that event to instance_terminator.go's 2s poll tick (async, decoupled from the transition); by contrast handleDeleteInstance does fire it synchronously.
note: Two independent artifact-tier dossier entries corroborate that instance-terminated must fire synchronously at the owning process's post-commit step; the doc's invariant already states this correctly. The kill/terminate HTTP path violates it by never attempting a synchronous fan-out, relying entirely on the async poll loop -- that is a code defect, not a doc error. Queued as fix-code; no doc change applied. Do not add the poll loop as a legitimate third firing site -- it is the failing path, not an intended one. Related to duplicate_of=43 in another cluster.

sources: dossier=Net position line 14 (host-agent-and-proxy, 2026-05-24, artifact) 'control-api for template/instance events and main-scope run-scope-terminal; the supervisor ... for sub-graph/fan-out-partition run-scope-terminal'; doc=lifecycle-subscriber.md pre-fix Boundaries/Invariants (lines 21,25) attributed run-scope-terminal to the supervisor exclusively while a separate Boundaries sentence already said 'two firers' -- internally inconsistent; code=controlapi/lifecycle.go CloseAndFanOutFrameRootRunScopesForInstance runs in control-api and fires run-scope-terminal for main/frame-root scopes on instance terminate/delete; runtime/lifecycle_fanout.go fires it from the supervisor for sub-graph exits.
note: Dossier is explicit and corroborated (two artifact-tier entries) that run-scope-terminal fires from whichever process closes that particular scope: control-api for main-scope closes tied to instance termination/deletion, supervisor for sub-graph/fan-out-partition closes. Doc mis-attributed it to the supervisor alone. Fixed Boundaries and the Invariants firing-site bullet to state the scope-kind split. Note: the parallel control-api cluster's already-applied fix to control-api.md still says 'the supervisor for run-scope-terminal events' / 'run-scope-terminal fan-out (fired by the supervisor when it closes a run scope)' -- that doc has NOT been brought fully in line with this scope-kind split and is now inconsistent with the corrected lifecycle-subscriber.md; flagging for a follow-up edit to control-api.md rather than touching it here.

sources: dossier=Net position line 12 (layer-crystallization, 2026-05-04, artifact) 'delivery is idempotent, keyed (peer-name, event-type, object-id) ... replays are no-ops'; Required behaviors line 21 (service-protocol-contract, 2026-05-04, artifact) 'idempotent delivery keyed (peer-name, event-type, object-id); replay is a no-op'; doc=lifecycle-subscriber.md pre-fix 'each (service, event) pair fires exactly once' and 'per-(service, event) ledger'; code=controlapi/lifecycle.go continues without the ledger upsert on subscriber error (re-fire on next pass), dispatch precedes the upsert (crash window re-fires), and the ledger row is keyed (service, scope-kind, scope-id) with an overwritten state column so legitimate re-transitions (redeploy, re-registration) re-fire the same callback.
note: The dossier's own stated delivery model is idempotent at-least-once (retry until recorded, replay of a *recorded* delivery is a no-op) plus legitimate re-fire on genuine re-transition -- not the doc's blanket exactly-once claim. Rewrote the invariant to state at-least-once + idempotent-handler requirement and re-fire-on-re-transition, and corrected the ledger key description in 'What it is' to (service, event type, object) matching the dossier's stated key shape.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors line 29 (host-agent-and-proxy, 2026-05-24, artifact-only) 'the lifecycle fan-out peer filter includes configured late_bind_service_proxies names when a template has late_bind_services, scoped to instance- and run-scope-keyed fan-out only (not template events)'; corroborated by design corpus concept host-agent-proxy (Boundaries: 'the per-instance service-bindings cache (populated via concept:lifecycle-subscriber)'), an independent artifact depending on this exact mechanism; doc=lifecycle-subscriber.md pre-fix Invariants described only template-referenced-peer fan-out, no mention of proxy augmentation or the template-vs-instance/run-scope asymmetry; code=controlapi/lifecycle.go LifecyclePeersForSpec appends LateBindServiceProxies for instance and run-scope fan-out but not for FanOutTemplateEvent.
note: Artifact-only dossier claim is corroborated by an independent design-corpus artifact (host-agent-proxy.md) that depends on the same mechanism, clearing the provenance gate. Added an invariant bullet documenting that instance- and run-scope-keyed fan-out additionally targets late-bound service proxies not named in the template, asymmetric with template events, citing concept:host-agent-proxy as the consumer.
